A.text:
Thank you for reading this.

As a child, I drew so lightly that my father had to tilt the paper toward the window. He always found something to ask about. The blue mark was a river. The small square was our house. I drew harder after that.

I think of that care when I put a few words in front of someone. Here is my small square of paper. Thank you for taking the time to see what I meant.

B.text:
Thank you for reading what I made.

In the kitchen, the first slice of bread always comes out crooked. Someone takes it before the neat slices reach the table, still warm enough to soften the butter.

I like that small kindness: receiving a thing before its maker has finished apologizing for it.

These words are my crooked slice. I am glad they reached you warm.

B.text:
Thank you for reading this little note.

I kept adding sentences to it, trying to make the thanks big enough. Then I read it again and began taking them out. There was more room around the words.

What I wanted to give you was a page that asked very little of you, with a few plain words on it: your care has reached someone. Mine is reaching back.
